clue.text: Police officers will accept promise to pay in full

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: cops are police officers
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt ('I owe you')

explanation.surface: Officers agree to take a debtor's pledge that the full amount will be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In full' is the definition: a copious account gives everything, in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something copious is plentiful and given in abundance, which is what 'in full' conveys of a supply.

clue.text: Coat from new catalogue? No thanks

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
no here means without, so the following word's letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A shopper turns down a coat from the latest mail-order brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T and A from the catalogue's letters, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a light hooded waterproof jacket, so it is a type of coat.

clue.text: Beg to include men beginning to talk in picture

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: to pray is to beg or entreat
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Plead to have the men start speaking in the film.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict them in a painting or performance, so it is a verb synonym of picture.

clue.text: Refuse to eat?

parts.note: surface reading: declining food, with refuse as a verb
setter's reading: refuse as a noun, waste matter that is nevertheless edible

explanation.walkthrough: Refuse switches from the verb (re-FUSE) to the noun (REF-use): leftover bits of a carcass that people still cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs of a slaughtered animal, once treated as waste but eaten as food.

clue.text: In some respect, a clever display

indicators.note: the solution lies inside some of the words that follow

parts.note: read across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A smart show earns some admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a visually striking public show, a synonym for a display.

clue.text: Consult an analyst — that bears fruit
Rate drug

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to grade a medicine; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means velocity and is also street slang for amphetamine, a stimulant drug.

clue.text: Relax with pork pie and a number of drinks

parts.note: pork pie is rhyming slang for lie
taken as written
a round is drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: Unwind in the pub with a pie and a few beers.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: pork pie (often 'porky') means a lie. A round is a set of drinks bought for everyone in a British pub group.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie around is to lounge idly, an informal way to say relax.

clue.text: "Bacon," I teased, "contains something poisonous"

indicators.note: the words before it hold the solution within them

parts.note: read across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A teasing remark that the breakfast meat holds a toxin.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a plant yielding a deadly toxin, so it is a poisonous thing.

clue.text: Enhance base of pizza with ground nutmeg

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, the last letter of the word

parts.note: its final letter

indicators.note: something ground is crushed, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Improve a pizza crust by grating some spice over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase or add to something, a synonym for enhance.

clue.text: Mistake to keep occasionally fiery animal

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is used

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An error leads to keeping some fiery creature now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is an African mammal, the tallest living animal, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Soon hero fell for Inga, according to insiders?

indicators.note: the insiders of words are their inner letters, so only the middles are taken

parts.note: the inner two letters
the inner two letters
the central letter
the inner two letters

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that a hero will shortly fall in love with Inga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to insiders' sounds like gossip from those in the know; it asks for the inside letters of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Erelong is an archaic adverb meaning before long, which is a synonym for soon.

clue.text: Run out, over the moon to be different

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
over the moon means delighted

explanation.surface: Someone's runs out of joy, delighted to stand apart from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' reads as a cricket dismissal, but 'out' rearranges just the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrelated things have no connection to each other, so they are distinct or different.

clue.text: Rubbish emptied in European river

indicators.note: a word emptied has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters
taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Waste has been dumped into a river on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major river of western Europe, flowing from Switzerland to the North Sea.

clue.text: Ultimately well-meaning type ruined country

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kindly sort of person ended up wrecking a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Study start of television broadcast about cycling event?

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so everything before it is read backwards

parts.note: a study is a den, and a den is a lair

indicators.note: 'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'television'

parts.note: its first letter
to emit a signal is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Look into the start of a TV programme about a bike race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' is a noun here, a private room; 'start of' picks the first letter of television.
explanation.definitionFit: A time trial is a race where cyclists ride alone against the clock, a standard cycling event.

clue.text: Large clubs put loner off

indicators.note: off can mean gone bad or out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Big golf clubs deterred a solitary player.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent describes a person who is fat or stout, a polite synonym for large in build.

clue.text: Home cider seen brewing

indicators.note: brewing means being mixed and fermented, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Homemade scrumpy has been spotted fermenting.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is the place where someone lives, a formal synonym for home.

clue.text: Unattractive companion missing members

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
arms are limbs, or members, so lacking them is armless

explanation.surface: A plain-looking friend is absent from the club roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' looks like people on a list, but here it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charmless lacks any appeal or charm, which makes it a synonym for unattractive.

clue.text: Opening of roof in centre court is right

indicators.note: in places one letter inside another word

parts.note: the core is the centre

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Opening the roof on Centre Court at Wimbledon is the right call.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is Wimbledon's main tennis court with a retractable roof; here the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and right are synonyms meaning accurate or true.

clue.text: In EastEnders ruin a party, finding something to smash?

parts.note: havoc means ruin; a Cockney drops the initial H
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: In the soap, a party is wrecked and something gets smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, so its characters drop their aitches. The definition refers to smashed avocado, a brunch staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is famously served crushed on toast as smashed avocado, so it is a fruit people smash.

clue.text: Retreat from Moscow?

parts.note: surface reading: Napoleon's disastrous withdrawal from Moscow in 1812
setter's reading: a country hideaway where Muscovites escape the city

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls a famous military withdrawal; read again, a retreat is a quiet holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country cottage, a weekend escape for city dwellers such as those from Moscow.

clue.text: Unusually cheap gold hat

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A golden hat going for a surprisingly low price.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is the French word for hat, used in English for headgear.

clue.text: Rather slow article by Italian poet

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A piece of writing by an Italian verse-maker is a bit sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: England cricketer, second to go in, bats on this?

indicators.note: going in means entering, so one letter is placed inside the name

parts.note: Joe Root, the England batsman and former captain
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An England cricketer coming in at number two wields the bat on this pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes 'bats' a verb for batting; it is the flying mammals, which hang up to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds or bats settle to sleep, which is where bats rest.

clue.text: Team, reportedly weary, keep trophies in here?

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so a word is chosen by how it sounds

parts.note: bored, a sense of weary, sounds like a plank of wood

explanation.surface: A tired team stores its cups here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a cabinet in a dining room where silverware or trophies might be displayed and stored.

clue.text: Disreputable prophet, not drinking, runs out on two separate occasions

indicators.note: out means removed, and two separate occasions means it happens once in each of two words

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
dry means abstaining from alcohol
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A shady fortune-teller, now teetotal, goes jogging twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On two separate occasions' means one R comes out of each word, not two from one.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means sordid or shabby in a squalid way, close to disreputable.

clue.text: Perhaps writer turned up for session

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means flipped bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as perhaps does
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A writer may show up for a sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of excess, especially drinking, and a session is British slang for such a bout.

clue.text: Inspect area in former colliery, say

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others around it

parts.note: ex- means former
A is the abbreviation for area
a colliery is an example of a mine

explanation.surface: Survey a section of an old coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to look at it closely, a direct synonym for inspect.

clue.text: Granny piercing material

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
a piercing wind or gaze is keen

explanation.surface: Grandma pushing a needle through cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally from Nanjing, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: One's pushed unpleasant person you once backed

parts.note: a troll is a nasty, hostile person, especially online

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone is shoved aside by a nasty character you used to support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's pushed' reads as a victim of bullying; it defines a cart that gets pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley is a wheeled cart that a shopper or porter pushes along.

clue.text: Carry out banker? Sweet!

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; the Exe flows through Devon
cute means sweet or charming

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to take away the bank worker, then cries 'Lovely!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is the crossword word for a river, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a plan or order is to perform it, which matches carry out as a synonym.
